summary.problem:
For deferred download with `st.download_button`, pipe errors to the script thread

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

If you use deferred download with `st.download_button`, there should be a way to catch errors that may be raised by the deferred generation function. Currently, if the funciton encounters an error, a warning message is displayed on the frontend and isn't accessible on the backend.

### Why?

When you use deferred download with `st.download_button`, the function which returns the download runs on its own thread so it won't block the script thread. This has two consequences:
1. There is no script context, so you can't use any Streamlit command, like `st.session_state`. (See #13337).
2. You can't handle errors raised by the deferred download function.

You can put try-catch blocks in your download function to avoid an unhandled error, but you can't really _do_ anything about it because you can't display a custom message or log something in Session State. (Maybe you could hack a solution by writing something to a temporary file on the server, but that doesn't seem ideal.)

### How?

A couple different solutions:
* Have the download button return an error if encountered so it can be caught in the main script.
* Give the download thread some (possibly restricted) script context (like #13337).
* Improve multithreading support more generally, and have some hook at the end of a script run to catch a session's child threads, like the download thread.

### Additional Context

_No response_

summary.problem:
st.tabs switches back to the first tab if an element is added or removed before the tabs

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Tabs should (and usually do) save their state between reruns so that if I adjust a widget inside a tab, that same tab stays visible.
However, if the rerun adds/removes a widget _above_ the tabs' declaration, the tab state is reset to the first tab no matter which tab was visible when the above-the-tabs widget was added/removed.


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

if "enabled" in st.session_state and st.session_state.enabled:
    st.button("Hi there!")

a, b = st.tabs(["Tab 1", "Tab 2"])

if "enabled_safe" in st.session_state and st.session_state.enabled_safe:
    st.button("Phew, safe!")

with a:
    st.write("Hello, world!")

with b:
    message = """Toggling the first switch will cause a button to
appear or disappear above the tabs. This causes the tabs to
reset to the first tab, incorrectly, in my opinion.

Toggling the second (safe) switch causes the button to appear
or disappear below the tabs, which preserves the tab state (correctly)."""
    st.write(message)
    enabled = st.toggle("Display it!", key="enabled")
    enabled_safe = st.toggle("This one's safe", key="enabled_safe")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Launch the provided code example
2. Open Tab 2 to reveal the toggles
3. Toggle the "Display it!" switch which will cause a new button to appear above the tabs
4. The tab will reset to Tab 1

I have experimented with a few different setups and it appears only adding/removing widgets causes this issue.
Simply changing the state of a widget (e.g. the label of a button) does not cause this issue.

### Expected Behavior

I expect that having a new button or other widget appear above a set of tabs
would not change which tab is currently visible.

### Current Behavior

See steps to reproduce.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.52.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Debian 3.12 Trixie (Docker)
- Browser: Brave (Chrome) (Brave 1.83.118 / Chromium: 141.0.7390.108)

summary.problem:
Incomplete type hint for date_input max_value: missing Literal["today"]

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hi,

It looks like the type hints for `st.date_input` are incomplete.

In `time_widgets.date_input`, the `max_value` parameter is typed as `SingleDateValue`, but the function also accepts the string literal `"today"`, as documented and supported at runtime.

This causes static type checkers (e.g. mypy, pyright, pylance) to raise errors even though the code is valid.

Suggested fix:
Extend the type hint to include Literal["today"]
This likely affects min_value as well.

Thanks!

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.date_input(
    "Select a date",
    max_value="today",
)
```

Add support for PyCapsule

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add support in Streamlit’s data APIs (e.g. st.dataframe, charts) for consuming objects that implement [Apache Arrow’s PyCapsule](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/CDataInterface/PyCapsuleInterface.html) C data interface (via `__arrow_c_schema__`, `__arrow_c_array__`, `__arrow_c_stream__`, etc.), so that Arrow-compatible tables/streams from any library can be passed in without requiring a hard dependency on PyArrow or extra data copies. This would enable zero-copy interoperability with other Arrow-based ecosystems (including potential device-backed data via the device variants of these methods) and make Streamlit more future-proof as more Python libraries adopt this standardized Arrow PyCapsule protocol.

### Additional Context

- https://github.com/vega/altair/issues/3568#issue-2506363561
- https://github.com/narwhals-dev/narwhals/pull/1181
- https://github.com/microsoft/LightGBM/issues/6204#issuecomment-2256015538
- Comparison to Dataframe Interchange Protocol: https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/CDataInterface/PyCapsuleInterface.html#comparison-to-dataframe-interchange-protocol

```python
def arrow_table_from_dfi_dataframe(dfi_df: DataFrameLike) -> pa.Table: 
     """Convert a DataFrame Interchange Protocol compatible object to an Arrow Table.""" 
     import pyarrow as pa 
  
     # First check if the dataframe object has a method to convert to arrow. 
     # Give this preference over the pyarrow from_dataframe function since the object 
     # has more control over the conversion, and may have broader compatibility. 
     # This is the case for Polars, which supports Date32 columns in direct conversion 
     # while pyarrow does not yet support this type in from_dataframe 
     for convert_method_name in ("arrow", "to_arrow", "to_arrow_table", "to_pyarrow"): 
         convert_method = getattr(dfi_df, convert_method_name, None) 
         if callable(convert_method): 
```

    # pa.table() will automatically check for `__arrow_c_stream__` and call that
    # todo: add pyarrow version check; I forget which version added support for the PyCapsule Interface
    return pa.table(dfi_df)

summary.problem:
File upload fails on Android mobile browsers

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When trying to upload a PDF file, it fails, and instead shows "connecting" 1 second and gets back to initial state. 
This issue doesn't always happen, but in general, I need to re-attempt several times to make the upload work.
It happens even with small pdf files (<200kB)

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.title("Simple PDF Upload Test")

# File uploader for PDF files only
uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("Choose a PDF file", type=["pdf"])

if uploaded_file is not None:
    # Success message
    st.success(f"✅ File uploaded: **{uploaded_file.name}**")
    
    # Display file details
    st.write(f"**Size:** {uploaded_file.size:,} bytes")
    
    # Optional: Show file type and other metadata
    st.write(f"**MIME Type:** {uploaded_file.type}")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Upload pdf file 

### Expected Behavior

File uploaded (works sometimes, after repeated attempts)

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

### Current Behavior

Tap "Choose a PDF" → select file.
- **WebSocket drops instantly**.
- Server logs show **repeated connect/disconnect cycles**.

2025-10-31 09:36:32.729 DEBUG Received the following back message: rerun_script { ... }
2025-10-31 09:36:32.729 DEBUG Beginning script thread
2025-10-31 09:36:32.730 DEBUG Disconnecting files for session...
2025-10-31 09:36:32.730 DEBUG Runtime state: ONE_OR_MORE_SESSIONS_CONNECTED → NO_SESSIONS_CONNECTED
2025-10-31 09:36:40.831 DEBUG Runtime state: NO_SESSIONS_CONNECTED → ONE_OR_MORE_SESSIONS_CONNECTED
2025-10-31 09:36:47.998 DEBUG Runtime state: ONE_OR_MORE_SESSIONS_CONNECTED → NO_SESSIONS_CONNECTED

... (repeats rapidly during upload attempt)

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]


### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- **Streamlit version**: `1.51.0`
- **Python version**: `3.12.3`
- **Operating system**: Ubuntu on **AWS EC2 t3.small**
- **Browsers**: 
- **Chrome on Android (mobile)** – Version 139.0.7258.62
- Firefox 141.0.1
- Lemur 2.7.3.013

Command: streamlit run test_upload.py --server.port=8501
Instance: AWS EC2 t3.small (2 vCPU, 2 GB RAM)
Network: Public IP, port 8501 ope

Allow uploading images from camera in `st.chat_input`

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Allow to upload images directly from the device camera or photo gallery. 

### Why?

_No response_

### How?

This might be as easy as adding `capture` to the `accept` whenever the image type is configured to `image`, `video`, or `audio` mime type. This allows to capture data from camera, microphone or camcorder if available.

- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/73162311/input-accept-image-capture-camera-allows-any-file-type-on-mobile

### Additional Context

- Maybe also support this for `st.file_uploader`?

summary.problem:
libodbc2 conflicts with preinstalled libodbc1 from Microsoft in Streamlit Cloud

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Trying to install `libodbc2` fails with the following message:

```
dpkg: error processing archive /tmp/apt-dpkg-install-NKXxq6/218-libodbc2_2.3.11-2+deb12u1_amd64.deb (--unpack):
 trying to overwrite '/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libodbc.so.2.0.0', which is also in package libodbc1:amd64 2.3.11-3
```

This shouldn't happen since `libodbc1` should be just a transitional package depending on `libodbc2`, but this specific version comes from the Microsoft repositories and doesn't do that.

1. Set up a github repository with any trivial, "Hello world"-like streamlit app.
2.  Add a `packages.txt` and put just `libodbc2` in it.
3. Try to deploy to Streamlit Cloud

The application is succesfully deployed.

summary.problem:
Make three dots menu in `st.dataframe` keyboard accessible

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

The three dots menu in a header of `st.dataframe` is not keyboard accessible when tabbing through the app. It should be, regardless of whether the header is hovered or not. Note that we want to revisit best practices for this as part of a bigger accessibility push before fixing this. Some other popular datagrid libraries (e.g. AgGrid) do not expose this element for keyboard navigation since data grids already contain a lot of clickable elements.

summary.problem:
Show top bar background only when needed (similar to ChatGPT)

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

ChatGPT has a pretty nice UX for their top bar: If the window is wide enough to show the elements on the top left/right without blocking the page content, the top bar doesn't have a background. Only if they would overlap the page content, the top bar gets a white background (and a gray border). 

Maybe we should try something similar? Given that our top bar is very similar, with some things on the top left and top right but not much in between. 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a194f1b9-6bd4-460f-a348-bd6165ccd008

### Why?

- Nicer UX. 
- More available screen height for the page content. 

### How?

Similar to ChatGPT but without the gray border. We'd definitely need to try this out to see if it feels good. Also need to see how this interacts with `st.navigation(..., position="top")`. 

### Additional Context

_No response_

summary.problem:
cache_data failing to serialize classes from v1.44.0

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I noticed in the upgrade from 1.43.0 to 1.44.0 that we are getting UnserializableReturnValueError when calling cache_data with a self defined class. I can confirm pickle dumps and loads works fine for this class when I run it outside of streamlit. 

Full error:
> streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_errors.UnserializableReturnValueError: Cannot serialize the return value (of type __main__.Example) in test(). st.cache_data uses pickle to serialize the function's return value and safely store it in the cache without mutating the original object. Please convert the return value to a pickle-serializable type. If you want to cache unserializable objects such as database connections or Tensorflow sessions, use st.cache_resource instead (see our docs for differences).

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
from streamlit import cache_data
import datetime as dt

class Example:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name

@cache_data(ttl=dt.timedelta(minutes=60))
def test():
    name = "andy"
    return Example(name)

if __name__ == '__main__':

    b = test()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Run the code above in streamlit

### Expected Behavior

The class should be pickled and be stored in the cache

### Current Behavior

_No response_

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.44.0
- Python version: 3.10
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_

### Summary

I noticed in the upgrade from 1.43.0 to 1.44.0 that we are getting UnserializableReturnValueError when calling cache_data with a self defined class. I can confirm pickle dumps and loads works fine for this class when I run it outside of streamlit. 

Full error:
> streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_errors.UnserializableReturnValueError: Cannot serialize the return value (of type __main__.Example) in test(). st.cache_data uses pickle to serialize the function's return value and safely store it in the cache without mutating the original object. Please convert the return value to a pickle-serializable type. If you want to cache unserializable objects such as database connections or Tensorflow sessions, use st.cache_resource instead (see our docs for differences).

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
from streamlit import cache_data
import datetime as dt

class Example:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name

@cache_data(ttl=dt.timedelta(minutes=60))
def test():
    name = "andy"
    return Example(name)

if __name__ == '__main__':

    b = test()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Run the code above in streamlit

### Expected Behavior

The class should be pickled and be stored in the cache

### Current Behavior

_No response_

- Python version: 3.10
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Chrome

https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/after-upload-file-stays-in-ram/119453/2

Streamlit Version 1.49.1
Python Version 3.13.7

I searched for the issue on all known databases without success

I am facing the following issue with st.file_uploader:

When I am uploading a File about 600MB the RAM usage is after I selected the File about 660 MB.
At the moment I pressed the upload button the RAM usage increases up to 1800MB.
After the Upload is done, the RAM usage stays at 660MB.
If I close the browsertab it stays at 660MB, only when I close the streamlit instance the RAM gets free.

I tryed several solutions:

clear_on_submit=True
working with session state keys
gc.collect()
st.rerun()

The phenomenon is:
If I set the clear_on_submit=false and deactivate the st.rerun() I am able to delete the File in the Widget and only then the file gets deleted from the RAM.

I tested it with a simple Upload code with the same result in different browsers on 2 different PCs and different streamlit versions.

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When `@st.cache_data` decorates a method that returns a custom class instance, `pickle.dumps()` intermittently fails with `PicklingError: Can't pickle <class 'X'>: it's not the same object as X`. This happens because Streamlit's `LocalSourcesWatcher` deletes watched modules from `sys.modules` on file changes, creating a class identity mismatch between the instance being pickled and the class found by pickle's resolution mechanism.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
### `repro_model.py`


"""Local module — simulates any user-defined class in a local .py file."""

class MyResult:
    def __init__(self, output: str = "", value: int = 0):
        self.output = output
        self.value = value


### `repro_agent.py`


"""
Helper module imported once by repro.py.
Simulates agents/__init__.py — only loaded once, holds a stale class reference
after sys.modules is invalidated by the file watcher.
"""
import streamlit as st
from repro_model import MyResult  # bound once at import time


@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False)
def get_result(key: str) -> MyResult:
    import time
    time.sleep(0.1)
    return MyResult(output=f"result for {key}", value=42)


### `repro.py` — run with `streamlit run repro.py`


import streamlit as st
import sys
import importlib
import repro_agent  # imported once — simulates agents/__init__.py


st.title("cache_data pickle race condition repro")

if st.button("1) Normal call (works)"):
    try:
        result = repro_agent.get_result("test")
        st.success(f"Got: {result.output}")
    except Exception as e:
        st.error(f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")

if st.button("2) Simulate file-watcher then call (fails, and keeps failing)"):
    # This is exactly what LocalSourcesWatcher.on_path_changed does:

        del sys.modules["repro_model"]

    # Re-import creates a NEW class object in sys.modules
    importlib.import_module("repro_model")

    # Clear cache so pickle.dumps is attempted again
    repro_agent.get_result.clear()

<details>

services:

    build:

    init: true

      - .:/app:ro
    entrypoint: ["/usr/bin/env", "streamlit", "run"]

```

</details>
<details>
<summary>./comp.py</summary>

```python
# comp.py

import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import streamlit as st

st_comp_get_cookies = st.components.v2.component(
    "component_bidi_drop_bug.get_cookies",
    js="""
    export default function(component){
        const { data, setTriggerValue } = component;
        console.log("Comp Instantiated: " + data._);
        // More advanced logic here
        const retObj = document.cookie;
        console.log("cookie-getter:", retObj);
        if(retObj !== undefined) setTriggerValue("get_cookies", retObj);
    }
    """,
    isolate_styles=False,
)

def _frame_gen(frame, skip=0):
    while frame:
        if frame.f_code.co_filename.startswith("/app"):
            if skip <= 0:
                yield frame
            else:
                skip -= 1
        frame = frame.f_back

_cwd = Path.cwd()

def _rm_cwd(path):
    if _cwd in Path(path).parents:
        return str(Path(path).relative_to(_cwd))
    return path

def unique_key(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return "".join(reversed([
        f"{_rm_cwd(f.f_code.co_filename)}-{f.f_code.co_name}-{f.f_lineno};"
        for f in _frame_gen(sys._getframe(), skip + 1)
    ])) + suffix

def unique_line_time(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return unique_key(suffix, skip + 1) + f":{int(datetime.now().timestamp())}"
```

summary.problem:
For deferred download with `st.download_button`, pipe errors to the script thread

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

If you use deferred download with `st.download_button`, there should be a way to catch errors that may be raised by the deferred generation function. Currently, if the funciton encounters an error, a warning message is displayed on the frontend and isn't accessible on the backend.

### Why?

When you use deferred download with `st.download_button`, the function which returns the download runs on its own thread so it won't block the script thread. This has two consequences:
1. There is no script context, so you can't use any Streamlit command, like `st.session_state`. (See #13337).
2. You can't handle errors raised by the deferred download function.

You can put try-catch blocks in your download function to avoid an unhandled error, but you can't really _do_ anything about it because you can't display a custom message or log something in Session State. (Maybe you could hack a solution by writing something to a temporary file on the server, but that doesn't seem ideal.)

### How?

A couple different solutions:
* Have the download button return an error if encountered so it can be caught in the main script.
* Give the download thread some (possibly restricted) script context (like #13337).
* Improve multithreading support more generally, and have some hook at the end of a script run to catch a session's child threads, like the download thread.

### Additional Context

_No response_

summary.problem:
st.tabs switches back to the first tab if an element is added or removed before the tabs

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Tabs should (and usually do) save their state between reruns so that if I adjust a widget inside a tab, that same tab stays visible.
However, if the rerun adds/removes a widget _above_ the tabs' declaration, the tab state is reset to the first tab no matter which tab was visible when the above-the-tabs widget was added/removed.


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

if "enabled" in st.session_state and st.session_state.enabled:
    st.button("Hi there!")

a, b = st.tabs(["Tab 1", "Tab 2"])

if "enabled_safe" in st.session_state and st.session_state.enabled_safe:
    st.button("Phew, safe!")

with a:
    st.write("Hello, world!")

with b:
    message = """Toggling the first switch will cause a button to
appear or disappear above the tabs. This causes the tabs to
reset to the first tab, incorrectly, in my opinion.

Toggling the second (safe) switch causes the button to appear
or disappear below the tabs, which preserves the tab state (correctly)."""
    st.write(message)
    enabled = st.toggle("Display it!", key="enabled")
    enabled_safe = st.toggle("This one's safe", key="enabled_safe")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Launch the provided code example
2. Open Tab 2 to reveal the toggles
3. Toggle the "Display it!" switch which will cause a new button to appear above the tabs
4. The tab will reset to Tab 1

I have experimented with a few different setups and it appears only adding/removing widgets causes this issue.
Simply changing the state of a widget (e.g. the label of a button) does not cause this issue.

### Expected Behavior

I expect that having a new button or other widget appear above a set of tabs
would not change which tab is currently visible.

### Current Behavior

See steps to reproduce.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3a172ba-92e2-4ec7-bcea-6d1ec0fde7b9

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.52.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Debian 3.12 Trixie (Docker)
- Browser: Brave (Chrome) (Brave 1.83.118 / Chromium: 141.0.7390.108)


### Additional Information

summary.problem:
st.tabs switches back to the first tab if an element is added or removed before the tabs

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Tabs should (and usually do) save their state between reruns so that if I adjust a widget inside a tab, that same tab stays visible.
However, if the rerun adds/removes a widget _above_ the tabs' declaration, the tab state is reset to the first tab no matter which tab was visible when the above-the-tabs widget was added/removed.


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

if "enabled" in st.session_state and st.session_state.enabled:
    st.button("Hi there!")

a, b = st.tabs(["Tab 1", "Tab 2"])

if "enabled_safe" in st.session_state and st.session_state.enabled_safe:
    st.button("Phew, safe!")

with a:
    st.write("Hello, world!")

with b:
    message = """Toggling the first switch will cause a button to
appear or disappear above the tabs. This causes the tabs to
reset to the first tab, incorrectly, in my opinion.

Toggling the second (safe) switch causes the button to appear
or disappear below the tabs, which preserves the tab state (correctly)."""
    st.write(message)
    enabled = st.toggle("Display it!", key="enabled")
    enabled_safe = st.toggle("This one's safe", key="enabled_safe")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Launch the provided code example
2. Open Tab 2 to reveal the toggles
3. Toggle the "Display it!" switch which will cause a new button to appear above the tabs
4. The tab will reset to Tab 1

I have experimented with a few different setups and it appears only adding/removing widgets causes this issue.
Simply changing the state of a widget (e.g. the label of a button) does not cause this issue.

### Expected Behavior

I expect that having a new button or other widget appear above a set of tabs
would not change which tab is currently visible.

### Current Behavior

See steps to reproduce.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3a172ba-92e2-4ec7-bcea-6d1ec0fde7b9

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.52.1
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Debian 3.12 Trixie (Docker)
- Browser: Brave (Chrome) (Brave 1.83.118 / Chromium: 141.0.7390.108)


### Additional Information

Hi,

In `time_widgets.date_input`, the `max_value` parameter is typed as `SingleDateValue`, but the function also accepts the string literal `"today"`, as documented and supported at runtime.

This causes static type checkers (e.g. mypy, pyright, pylance) to raise errors even though the code is valid.

Suggested fix:
Extend the type hint to include Literal["today"]
This likely affects min_value as well.

Thanks!

summary.problem:
st.data_editor infer empty column as Multiselect column instead of Text column

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

st.data_editor infer empty column as Multiselect column instead of Text column. As a result, text input in a cell of an empty column is stored in a list in the underlying pandas DataFrame. For example, entering `"my value"` results to `["my value"]` in the DataFrame cell. Even explicitly configuring the column as Text column with `st.column_config.TextColumn` does not work. The bug is introduced by the recent 1.52.0 release. I believe it's due to this change:
```
if column_data_kind in (ColumnDataKind.LIST, ColumnDataKind.EMPTY):
            return list(value) if is_list_like(value) else [value]  # ty: ignore 
```
From this merged PR:
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/12935/files

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

df = pd.DataFrame([{'a': None}])

modified_df = st.data_editor(df)

print(modified_df)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

Input "text" should set the text in the DataFrame cell, not a list. 

### Current Behavior

Currently, input "text" set ["text"] instead of "text" in the DataFrame cell. 

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.52.1 and 1.52.0
- Python version: 3.13.2
- Operating System: Windows 
- Browser: Chrome 


### Additional Information

_No response_

summary.problem:
Add support for PyCapsule

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add support in Streamlit’s data APIs (e.g. st.dataframe, charts) for consuming objects that implement [Apache Arrow’s PyCapsule](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/CDataInterface/PyCapsuleInterface.html) C data interface (via `__arrow_c_schema__`, `__arrow_c_array__`, `__arrow_c_stream__`, etc.), so that Arrow-compatible tables/streams from any library can be passed in without requiring a hard dependency on PyArrow or extra data copies. This would enable zero-copy interoperability with other Arrow-based ecosystems (including potential device-backed data via the device variants of these methods) and make Streamlit more future-proof as more Python libraries adopt this standardized Arrow PyCapsule protocol.

### Additional Context

- https://github.com/vega/altair/issues/3568#issue-2506363561
- https://github.com/narwhals-dev/narwhals/pull/1181
- https://github.com/microsoft/LightGBM/issues/6204#issuecomment-2256015538
- Comparison to Dataframe Interchange Protocol: https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/CDataInterface/PyCapsuleInterface.html#comparison-to-dataframe-interchange-protocol

```python

     """Convert a DataFrame Interchange Protocol compatible object to an Arrow Table.""" 
     import pyarrow as pa 
  
     # First check if the dataframe object has a method to convert to arrow. 
     # Give this preference over the pyarrow from_dataframe function since the object 
     # has more control over the conversion, and may have broader compatibility. 
     # This is the case for Polars, which supports Date32 columns in direct conversion 
     # while pyarrow does not yet support this type in from_dataframe 
     for convert_method_name in ("arrow", "to_arrow", "to_arrow_table", "to_pyarrow"): 
         convert_method = getattr(dfi_df, convert_method_name, None)

```

summary.problem:
File upload fails on Android mobile browsers

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When trying to upload a PDF file, it fails, and instead shows "connecting" 1 second and gets back to initial state. 
This issue doesn't always happen, but in general, I need to re-attempt several times to make the upload work.
It happens even with small pdf files (<200kB)

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.title("Simple PDF Upload Test")

# File uploader for PDF files only
uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("Choose a PDF file", type=["pdf"])

if uploaded_file is not None:
    # Success message
    st.success(f"✅ File uploaded: **{uploaded_file.name}**")
    
    # Display file details
    st.write(f"**Size:** {uploaded_file.size:,} bytes")
    
    # Optional: Show file type and other metadata
    st.write(f"**MIME Type:** {uploaded_file.type}")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Upload pdf file 

### Expected Behavior

File uploaded (works sometimes, after repeated attempts)

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]

### Current Behavior

Tap "Choose a PDF" → select file.
- **WebSocket drops instantly**.
- Server logs show **repeated connect/disconnect cycles**.

2025-10-31 09:36:32.729 DEBUG Received the following back message: rerun_script { ... }
2025-10-31 09:36:32.729 DEBUG Beginning script thread
2025-10-31 09:36:32.730 DEBUG Disconnecting files for session...
2025-10-31 09:36:32.730 DEBUG Runtime state: ONE_OR_MORE_SESSIONS_CONNECTED → NO_SESSIONS_CONNECTED
2025-10-31 09:36:40.831 DEBUG Runtime state: NO_SESSIONS_CONNECTED → ONE_OR_MORE_SESSIONS_CONNECTED
2025-10-31 09:36:47.998 DEBUG Runtime state: ONE_OR_MORE_SESSIONS_CONNECTED → NO_SESSIONS_CONNECTED

... (repeats rapidly during upload attempt)

[IMAGE OMITTED: not inspected]


### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- **Streamlit version**: `1.51.0`
- **Python version**: `3.12.3`
- **Operating system**: Ubuntu on **AWS EC2 t3.small**
- **Browsers**: 
- **Chrome on Android (mobile)** – Version 139.0.7258.62
- Firefox 141.0.1
- Lemur 2.7.3.013

Command: streamlit run test_upload.py --server.port=8501
Instance: AWS EC2 t3.small (2 vCPU, 2 GB RAM)
Network: Public IP, port 8501 ope

_No response_

### Summary

I am using st.file_uploader to upload ~3.5gb file into my streamlit dashboard. This however, results in the server getting killed.
When I inspect using btop, Upon file upload, the server starts using an astronomic amount of RAM.

EDIT: I tried imposing a RAM limit by dockerizing the dashboard and settting a 4gb RAM limit, but it just gets killed in the container.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("Choose a video file", type=["mp4", "mov", "avi"])
```


### Steps To Reproduce

streamlit run dashboard.py --maxUploadSize=5000

### Expected Behavior

It's probably better to stream it in chunks to disk when clicking an 'upload file' button.

### Current Behavior

The server gets killed.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

```text
- `st.cache_data` is the recommended way to cache computations that return data: loading a DataFrame from CSV, transforming a NumPy array, querying an API, or any other function that returns a serializable data object (str, int, float, DataFrame, array, list, …). It creates a new copy of the data at each function call, making it safe against [mutations and race conditions](#mutation-and-concurrency-issues). ```

محدودیت: مستندات رسمی `st.cache_data` به صراحت اشاره می‌کند که مقدار بازگشتی تابع باید قابل پیکل باشد و اگر اشیایی غیرقابل سریالی‌سازی بازگردانده شوند، این خطا به وجود می‌آید. همچنین اشاره شده است که در موارد اشیای غیرقابل سریالی‌سازی مانند اتصال‌های دیتابیس باید از `st.cache_resource` استفاده شود. اشکال گزارش شده در نسخه 1.44.0 نیز نشانگر تغییر در مدیریت کش و حساسیت نسبت به اشیای غیرسریالی‌پذیر است. بنابراین برای تحلیل دقیق‌تر باید مشاهده کرد آیا خروجی تابع واقعا قابل پیکل شدن هست یا خیر و اطلاعات بیشتر روی ساختار کلاس و خروجی آن مورد نیاز است.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: ممکن است اشیایی که برمی‌گردند قابل سریالی‌سازی با پیکل نباشند و این باعث خطای UnserializableReturnValueError شود.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: شاید تابع بازگردانده شده به صورت مستقیم یک کلاس تعریف شده خودکار باشد که streamlit قادر به سریالی‌سازی آن نیست.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: احتمالا استفاده نادرست از دکوراتور `st.cache_data` به همراه برگرداندن اشیای غیرقابل پیکل، موجب مشکل شده است.

وضعیت: رفع مشکل تأیید نشده است؛ ثبت پاسخ فقط پس از تأیید نگه‌دارنده انجام می‌شود.

summary.problem:
cache_data failing to serialize classes from v1.44.0

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I noticed in the upgrade from 1.43.0 to 1.44.0 that we are getting UnserializableReturnValueError when calling cache_data with a self defined class. I can confirm pickle dumps and loads works fine for this class when I run it outside of streamlit. 

Full error:
> streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_errors.UnserializableReturnValueError: Cannot serialize the return value (of type __main__.Example) in test(). st.cache_data uses pickle to serialize the function's return value and safely store it in the cache without mutating the original object. Please convert the return value to a pickle-serializable type. If you want to cache unserializable objects such as database connections or Tensorflow sessions, use st.cache_resource instead (see our docs for differences).

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
from streamlit import cache_data
import datetime as dt

class Example:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name

@cache_data(ttl=dt.timedelta(minutes=60))
def test():
    name = "andy"
    return Example(name)

if __name__ == '__main__':

    b = test()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Run the code above in streamlit

### Expected Behavior

The class should be pickled and be stored in the cache

### Current Behavior

_No response_

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.44.0
- Python version: 3.10
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_

summary.problem:
cache_data failing to serialize classes from v1.44.0

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

I noticed in the upgrade from 1.43.0 to 1.44.0 that we are getting UnserializableReturnValueError when calling cache_data with a self defined class. I can confirm pickle dumps and loads works fine for this class when I run it outside of streamlit. 

Full error:
> streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_errors.UnserializableReturnValueError: Cannot serialize the return value (of type __main__.Example) in test(). st.cache_data uses pickle to serialize the function's return value and safely store it in the cache without mutating the original object. Please convert the return value to a pickle-serializable type. If you want to cache unserializable objects such as database connections or Tensorflow sessions, use st.cache_resource instead (see our docs for differences).

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
from streamlit import cache_data
import datetime as dt

class Example:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name

@cache_data(ttl=dt.timedelta(minutes=60))
def test():
    name = "andy"
    return Example(name)

if __name__ == '__main__':

    b = test()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Run the code above in streamlit

### Expected Behavior

The class should be pickled and be stored in the cache

### Current Behavior

_No response_

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.44.0
- Python version: 3.10
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_
summary.rationale: مستندات رسمی `st.cache_data` به صراحت اشاره می‌کند که مقدار بازگشتی تابع باید قابل پیکل باشد و اگر اشیایی غیرقابل سریالی‌سازی بازگردانده شوند، این خطا به وجود می‌آید. همچنین اشاره شده است که در موارد اشیای غیرقابل سریالی‌سازی مانند اتصال‌های دیتابیس باید از `st.cache_resource` استفاده شود. اشکال گزارش شده در نسخه 1.44.0 نیز نشانگر تغییر در مدیریت کش و حساسیت نسبت به اشیای غیرسریالی‌پذیر است. بنابراین برای تحلیل دقیق‌تر باید مشاهده کرد آیا خروجی تابع واقعا قابل پیکل شدن هست یا خیر و اطلاعات بیشتر روی ساختار کلاس و خروجی آن مورد نیاز است.

sources.quote:
Cached objects are stored in "pickled" form, which means that the return
value of a cached function must be pickleable. Each caller of the cached
function gets its own copy of the cached data.

A function's arguments must be hashable to cache it. If you have an
unhashable argument (like a database connection) or an argument you
want to exclude from caching, use an underscore prefix in the argument
name. In this case, Streamlit will return a cached value when all other
arguments match a previous function call. Alternatively, you can
declare custom hashing functions with ``hash_funcs``.

- `st.cache_data` is the recommended way to cache computations that return data: loading a DataFrame from CSV, transforming a NumPy array, querying an API, or any other function that returns a serializable data object (str, int, float, DataFrame, array, list, …). It creates a new copy of the data at each function call, making it safe against [mutations and race conditions](#mutation-and-concurrency-issues). The behavior of `st.cache_data` is what you want in most cases – so if you're unsure, start with `st.cache_data` and see if it works!

Please note that file uploader is a **bit problematic** because

محدودیت: مطابق مستندات و مسائل موجود در مرجع‌ها، ویجت `file_uploader` فقط یک فایل را هر بار آپلود می‌کند و فایل‌ها در RAM نگهداری می‌شوند. حذف فایل از ویجت معمولاً باعث آزاد شدن حافظه می‌شود اما به نظر می‌رسد پاکسازی کامل در حالت معمول انجام نمی‌شود. همچنین دوبار اجرا شدن callback هنگام آپلود فایل جدید می‌تواند باعث مصرف حافظه بالاتر و باقی ماندن فایل‌ها در RAM شود. نیاز به جزئیات بیشتر درباره پیاده‌سازی داخلی و تعامل با حافظه است تا بتوان علت دقیق را تعیین کرد.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: فایل‌های آپلود شده در RAM باقی می‌مانند به دلیل رفتار طبیعی ویجت `st.file_uploader` که فایل‌ها را نگهداری می‌کند تا امکان دسترسی به آنها در جلسات بعد وجود داشته باشد.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: امکان پاک شدن برنامه‌ریزی شده ویجت فایل آپلودر وجود ندارد و نیازمند مکانیزم دیگری برای آزادسازی حافظه است.

فرضیهٔ تأییدنشده: دوبار اجرا شدن callback هنگام آپلود مجدد فایل ممکن است به دلیل مکانیزم داخلی تغییر فایل در ویجت باشد که باعث افزایش مصرف حافظه می‌شود.

وضعیت: رفع مشکل تأیید نشده است؛ ثبت پاسخ فقط پس از تأیید نگه‌دارنده انجام می‌شود.

Streamlit Version 1.49.1
Python Version 3.13.7

I searched for the issue on all known databases without success

I am facing the following issue with st.file_uploader:

When I am uploading a File about 600MB the RAM usage is after I selected the File about 660 MB.
At the moment I pressed the upload button the RAM usage increases up to 1800MB.
After the Upload is done, the RAM usage stays at 660MB.
If I close the browsertab it stays at 660MB, only when I close the streamlit instance the RAM gets free.

clear_on_submit=True
working with session state keys
gc.collect()
st.rerun()

sources.quote:
Please note that file uploader is a **bit problematic** because
- You can only upload one file at the time.
- You get no additional information on the file like name, size, upload time, type etc. So you
cannot distinguish the files without reading the content.
- every time you interact with any widget, the script is rerun and you risk processing or storing
the file again!
- The file uploader widget is not cleared when you clear the cache and there is no way to clear the
file uploader widget programmatically.

- You can only upload one file at the time.
- You get no additional information on the file like name, size, upload time, type etc. So you
cannot distinguish the files without reading the content. The python object id changes for each script rerun so you cannot use that either.
- every time you interact with any widget, the script is rerun and you risk processing or storing
the file again!
- The file uploader widget is not cleared when you clear the cache and there is no way to clear the
file uploader widget programmatically.

On each subsequent upload after the first upload, the `on_change` callback is called twice. My understanding is that uploading a new file also clears the existing file, triggering another callback execution. In that sense, this behavior might be a feature, not a bug. Nonetheless, this behavior can be confusing and unintuitive.

2026-09-01T18:51:38Z
```

متن شاهد:

```text
Our incident: a `data=callable` on `st.download_button` called into functions that (transitively) read `@st.cache_data`-cached helpers. Because those calls run outside `ScriptRunContext`, they picked up cached results from a *different* request context — users occasionally downloaded a file that didn't match what they'd just generated on screen, with nothing in the logs to explain why. We only found the mechanism by tracing the full call graph of the callable, not just inspecting it — a lambda that looks pure can still be unsafe if anything it calls touches cached/session state indirectly.
```

summary.problem:
st.cache_data on class methods intermittently raises UnserializableReturnValueError

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

When `@st.cache_data` decorates a method that returns a custom class instance, `pickle.dumps()` intermittently fails with `PicklingError: Can't pickle <class 'X'>: it's not the same object as X`. This happens because Streamlit's `LocalSourcesWatcher` deletes watched modules from `sys.modules` on file changes, creating a class identity mismatch between the instance being pickled and the class found by pickle's resolution mechanism.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
### `repro_model.py`


"""Local module — simulates any user-defined class in a local .py file."""

class MyResult:

sources.quote:
- **#12069** — [st.empty does not clear removed elements](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12069): Very likely a duplicate. Reports the same core behavior where `st.empty()` containers fail to clear old elements if new content has fewer items, leaving ghost elements visible. Confirmed bug, P3.
- **#10126** — [`st.close()` or `st.end()` to remove stale elements mid-run](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/10126): A feature request that directly addresses the underlying limitation. Proposes a mechanism to explicitly discard remaining stale elements within a container before the script run finishes, which would solve this issue.

Confirming this from a production incident — and it's a bit worse than "missing ScriptRunContext produces a warning": inside that thread, `st.session_state` reads return stale values and `@st.cache_data`-wrapped calls silently return whatever was already cached, **with no error and no warning**. Both just look like they worked.

Our incident: a `data=callable` on `st.download_button` called into functions that (transitively) read `@st.cache_data`-cached helpers. Because those calls run outside `ScriptRunContext`, they picked up cached results from a *different* request context — users occasionally downloaded a file that didn't match what they'd just generated on screen, with nothing in the logs to explain why. We only found the mechanism by tracing the full call graph of the callable, not just inspecting it — a lambda that looks pure can still be unsafe if anything it calls touches cached/session state indirectly.

import sys
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

import streamlit as st

st_comp_get_cookies = st.components.v2.component(
    "component_bidi_drop_bug.get_cookies",
    js="""
    export default function(component){
        const { data, setTriggerValue } = component;
        console.log("Comp Instantiated: " + data._);
        // More advanced logic here
        const retObj = document.cookie;
        console.log("cookie-getter:", retObj);
        if(retObj !== undefined) setTriggerValue("get_cookies", retObj);
    }
    """,
    isolate_styles=False,
)

def _frame_gen(frame, skip=0):
    while frame:
        if frame.f_code.co_filename.startswith("/app"):
            if skip <= 0:
                yield frame
            else:
                skip -= 1
        frame = frame.f_back

_cwd = Path.cwd()

def _rm_cwd(path):
    if _cwd in Path(path).parents:
        return str(Path(path).relative_to(_cwd))
    return path

def unique_key(suffix: str = "", skip: int = 0) -> str:
    return "".join(reversed([
        f"{_rm_cwd(f.f_code.co_filename)}-{f.f_code.co_name}-{f.f_lineno};"
        for f in _frame_gen(sys._getframe(), skip + 1)
    ])) + suffix

    return unique_key(suffix, skip + 1) + f":{int(datetime.now().timestamp())}"
